_comment: Which frame from `npm run shoot` ships where. One list, because the same
frames feed four surfaces and they drifted apart: a new shot landed with no
home, a deleted frame stayed referenced, and the store set fell five weeks
behind the README set.
surfaces: readme = docs/screenshots/ (2880x1800, README.md)
landing = docs/index.html (reads the readme set's files)
store = docs/store-screenshots/ (1280x800, both extension stores
and the Microsoft Store listing)
`composed: true` means the frame is not photographed but built from others
(compose-tricolor.cjs), so the downscaler must not look for a source of the
same name. `sourceFor` names the frames a composed one is built from: they
are shot every run but ship nowhere themselves. A frame with `ships: []` is
also still shot every run — the shoot doubles as a UI smoke test — it just
must not sit committed in a shipped folder.
`reading` became one of those on 2026-08-08, when tricolor took over as the
opening frame everywhere. The rule behind that (Emil's): a frame that OPENS
a surface has to read as an application, so tricolor keeps its toolbar — and
since tricolor is composed FROM `reading`, `reading` has to keep its toolbar
too. The toolbar-less frame the copy needs is therefore `page_only`, shot
separately, and `reading` stayed on as a tricolor source only.
Read by scale-store-shots.cjs (what to downscale) and check-screenshots.mjs
(what must exist where).
